import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a comprehensive figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :2])
sensor_order = df.groupby('sensor_type')['price_usd'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', order=sensor_order, ax=ax1, palette='Set2')
ax1.set_title('Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Megapixels vs Price scatter plot with sensor type
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
sensor_types = df['sensor_type'].unique()
colors = sns.color_palette('tab10', n_colors=len(sensor_types))
for i, sensor in enumerate(sensor_types):
    subset = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax2.scatter(subset['megapixels'], subset['price_usd'], 
                alpha=0.6, s=30, label=sensor, color=colors[i])
ax2.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_title('Megapixels vs Price', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.legend(fontsize=7, loc='upper left')

# 3. Camera releases over years
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
year_counts = df['model_year'].value_counts().sort_index()
ax3.plot(year_counts.index, year_counts.values, marker='o', linewidth=2, markersize=5, color='steelblue')
ax3.fill_between(year_counts.index, year_counts.values, alpha=0.3, color='steelblue')
ax3.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=10)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=10)
ax3.set_title('Camera Releases by Year', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 4. 4K Video capability distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
video_counts = df['has_video_4k'].value_counts()
labels = ['No 4K', '4K Capable']
colors_pie = ['#ff9999', '#66b3ff']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax4.pie(video_counts.values, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%',
                                     colors=colors_pie, startangle=90)
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')
ax4.set_title('4K Video Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 5. Average price by brand (top 10 brands)
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10).index
brand_prices = df[df['brand'].isin(top_brands)].groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=True)
ax5.barh(brand_prices.index, brand_prices.values, color='coral')
ax5.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax5.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=10)
ax5.set_title('Avg Price by Top 10 Brands', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 6. Weight vs Price by body type
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
body_types = df['body_type'].unique()
for body in body_types:
    subset = df[df['body_type'] == body]
    ax6.scatter(subset['weight_grams'], subset['price_usd'], 
                alpha=0.6, s=40, label=body)
ax6.set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=10)
ax6.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax6.set_title('Weight vs Price by Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax6.legend(fontsize=8)

# 7. ISO performance distribution
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
ax7.hist(df['max_iso'], bins=30, color='mediumseagreen', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax7.set_xlabel('Max ISO', fontsize=10)
ax7.set_ylabel('Frequency', fontsize=10)
ax7.set_title('Distribution of Max ISO', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax7.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# 8. Lens mount distribution
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
mount_counts = df['lens_mount'].value_counts().head(8)
ax8.bar(range(len(mount_counts)), mount_counts.values, color='plum', edgecolor='black')
ax8.set_xticks(range(len(mount_counts)))
ax8.set_xticklabels(mount_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right')
ax8.set_xlabel('Lens Mount', fontsize=10)
ax8.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=10)
ax8.set_title('Top 8 Lens Mounts', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Overall title
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
